title: Cutting a closed subset while meeting locally closed pieces
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local ring of finite dimension [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and put $U=X\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$. Let $T\subseteq X$ be a nonempty closed subset of dimension $e\geq0$. Let $W_1,\ldots,W_s$ be a finite family of nonempty locally closed subsets of $U\setminus T$; the family is allowed to be empty. Then there exist $f_1,\ldots,f_e\in\mathfrak m$ such that $T\cap V(f_1,\ldots,f_e)=\{\mathfrak m\}$ and $W_j\cap V(f_1,\ldots,f_e)\ne\varnothing$ for every $1\leq j\leq s$. Here locally closed means the intersection of an open and a closed subset, and $V(f_1,\ldots,f_e)$ is the set of prime ideals containing every $f_i$.

source.place: Tag 0ECR (lemma-punctured-still-connected), prime-avoidance construction in the second half of the proof; closed points in the puncture are supplied by Morphisms Tag 02J6 (lemma-ubiquity-Jacobson-schemes), case (4).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], the closed subsets of the spectrum are exactly the sets $V(I)$. The radical formula in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] identifies its ideal of vanishing elements with $\sqrt I$ and reverses inclusion. An ascending chain of ideals stabilizes: its union is an ideal, whose finite generators, by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], all occur at one stage. Thus descending chains of closed subsets of $X$ stabilize, and the same holds in every closed subspace of $X$. These spaces are Noetherian in the topological sense (equivalently every nonempty collection of closed subsets has a minimal member).

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, second half of proof: inductive prime-avoidance slicing; details expanded by Q72.

proof.text: The open subset $U\setminus T$ of $U$ has the property that a locally closed subset of it is locally closed in $U$: write its closed part as the intersection with a closed subset of $U$, and intersect its open part with $U\setminus T$. Apply [lem-per-punctured-local-closed-points] to each $W_j$ and choose $w_j\in W_j$ closed in $U$. Write $\mathfrak p_j$ for its prime ideal. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], $V(\mathfrak p_j)\cap U=\{w_j\}$, and $\mathfrak p_j\subsetneq\mathfrak m$ gives $V(\mathfrak p_j)=\{w_j,\mathfrak m\}$. When $s=0$ no choices are made.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, second half of proof: inductive prime-avoidance slicing; details expanded by Q72.

proof.text: We construct, for $0\leq n\leq e$, elements $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in\mathfrak m$ belonging to every $\mathfrak p_j$, with $T_n=T\cap V(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ satisfying $\dim T_n\leq e-n$. Every nonempty closed subset of the local spectrum contains $\mathfrak m$: it contains a prime $\mathfrak q$, hence contains $V(\mathfrak q)\ni\mathfrak m$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. Thus all these cuts are nonempty. The base case is $T_0=T$ and the empty list. Fix $n<e$ and assume the invariant.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, second half of proof: inductive prime-avoidance slicing; details expanded by Q72.

proof.text:
By Step 1 and [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components], $T_n$ has finitely many irreducible components. They cover $T_n$: the closure of each point is irreducible, and successive strict enlargements to irreducible closed subsets must terminate, since by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] each enlargement extends a chain and $\dim T_n\leq e-n<\infty$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], each component is $V(\mathfrak q)$ for a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$. Keep only those components of positive dimension. Their primes satisfy $\mathfrak q

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, second half of proof: inductive prime-avoidance slicing; details expanded by Q72.

proof.text: Put $J=\mathfrak m\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^s\mathfrak p_j$, interpreting the empty intersection as $A$, so $J=\mathfrak m$ when $s=0$. For each positive-dimensional component prime $\mathfrak q$, choose $a\in\mathfrak m\setminus\mathfrak q$ and $b_j\in\mathfrak p_j\setminus\mathfrak q$. This is possible by Step 4 and $\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak m$. Then $a\prod_j b_j\in J\setminus\mathfrak q$: every factor avoids the prime $\mathfrak q$, and the product belongs to $\mathfrak m$ and to every $\mathfrak p_j$. Thus $J$ is contained in none of the finitely many component primes to avoid.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, second half of proof: inductive prime-avoidance slicing; details expanded by Q72.

proof.text: If there is at least one positive-dimensional component, apply [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] with ideal $J$ and exactly their finite list of prime ideals to choose $f_{n+1}\in J$ outside every one of them. All the avoided ideals are prime, as required by that lemma. If the list is empty, take $f_{n+1}=0$. In either case $f_{n+1}\in\mathfrak m\cap\bigcap_j\mathfrak p_j$ and no positive-dimensional component of $T_n$ is contained in $V(f_{n+1})$.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, second half of proof: inductive prime-avoidance slicing; details expanded by Q72.

proof.text: Let $k=e-n\geq1$ and consider any strict chain $Z_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq Z_r$ of irreducible closed subsets of $T_{n+1}=T_n\cap V(f_{n+1})$. Its top member lies in a component $C$ of $T_n$, by Step 4: an irreducible set contained in a finite union of closed sets is contained in one of them, by induction on the number of sets using the definition of irreducibility. If $\dim C=0$, the dimension definition gives $r=0\leq k-1$. Otherwise $C\not\subseteq V(f_{n+1})$, so $Z_r\subsetneq C$. Appending $C$ gives a chain of length $r+1$ in $T_n$; hence $r+1\leq\dim T_n\leq k$. This proves $\dim T_{n+1}\leq e-(n+1)$ directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and closes the induction. No equality in the dimension drop, catenarity, or purity of dimension is needed.

source.place: Tag 0ECR, lemma-punctured-still-connected, second half of proof: inductive prime-avoidance slicing; details expanded by Q72.

proof.text: At $n=e$, $T_e$ contains $\mathfrak m$ and has dimension at most zero. If it contained a prime $\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak m$, closedness would give $\{\mathfrak m\}\subsetneq V(\mathfrak q)\subseteq T_e$, a length-one chain of irreducible closed subsets by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], contradicting [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus $T_e=\{\mathfrak m\}$. Every $f_i$ belongs to every $\mathfrak p_j$, so $w_j\in W_j\cap V(f_1,\ldots,f_e)$. When $e=0$ the same dimension argument already gives $T=\{\mathfrak m\}$ and the empty list has zero locus $X$; when $s=0$ the meeting conditions are vacuous.
